newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil may exempt stocks from "check tax" - report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil may exempt stocks from "check tax" - report.

text.p: The Brazilian government is studying whether to exempt stock market transactions from the so-called CPMF check tax, the private Invest News agency reported.

Invest News, quoting Finance Ministry Executive Secretary Pedro Parente, said the government had no intention of ditching the 0.2 percent tax, due to be levied on all financial transactions after January 23.
The agency said Parente spoke to reporters in Congress.
Parente was not available to confirm the report and Finance Ministry officials said they had no comment.
The CPMF is designed to raise some 400 million reais a month to fund health services.
Share prices have edged upward over the past two days following comments by government officials that they feared the tax could provoke investors to flee Brazilian stock markets.
Parente said that "there is not the slightest chance the CPMF won't be implemented," Invest News said.
But he said there were concerns about the tax's impact on investors and the stock markets, adding that officials had not yet identified a mechanism that would neutralize the impact.
On Tuesday, Industry and Commerce Minister Francisco Dornelles criticized the tax, and a newspaper reported that Central Bank Director Gustavo Franco was also concerned about it.
